thread:
camille (arch): quick check — headerless clients are still hitting v1 endpoints after the migration flag flip; we're seeing increased KV cache churn on runtime nodes. thinking we can either add a tiny edge shim that injects a compatibility header (cheap) or push a strict deprecation: require X-RI-API-V from clients. opinions?

lee (eng-infra): can you paste the top-line metrics? is this CPU or memory pressure or just increased cache misses?

camille (arch): mostly cache misses and some p95 token-latency regressions. sample: cache hit ratio dropped from 86% -> 64% for a subset of tenants. no obvious CPU spike yet.

raj (runtime): if we add a shim at the edge it would be a small Envoy filter or nginx-lua snippet that sets a header when missing. downside: more logic at edge, slightly harder tracing. example shim: 
```
if not req.headers['X-RI-API-V'] then
  req.headers['X-RI-API-V'] = 'v1-compat'
  req.headers['X-RI-Injected'] = 'shim-v1-2026'
end
```

sara (observability): if we go shim route we need an explicit telemetry tag for injected vs native. please add a counter + trace attribute: compat.injected=true/false. otherwise we won't be able to deprecate later. also send deprecation warning header back to clients.

max (ops): ops concerns: shim adds ~2-4ms p50 cost in our EU edge tests. planable, but we need a tight canary + automatic rollback. rollout idea: 1% EU -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h with rollout triggers watching p95 latency, cache hit ratio, and error rate. rollback if p95 increases > 10% or cache hit ratio drops > 8%.

camille (arch): agreed. long-term we can't keep the shim forever. propose: shim + deprecation timeline: 90 days active shim + warning headers, 180 days hard deprecation notice to customers, 270 days auto-reject unless tenant opts into legacy flag. open to tweaking durations.

lee (eng-infra): +1 for shim + explicit timeline. also prefer the shim be feature-flagged at edge and runtime so we can kill quickly. add a tenant-level opt-out but default inject for unknown clients.

raj (runtime): we'll need unit tests for adaptor behavior (in runtime) and a synthetic load that measures KV cache contention churn. can we get a test harness that replays headerless traffic?

camille (arch): i'll assemble a small replay set from last week's traces (anonymized). raj, can you sketch the test harness requirements?

raj (runtime): simple: 1) baseline run current traffic against runtime without shim, 2) run against runtime behind shim, measure per-key cache eviction rate and tail latency. target: show <5% additional eviction rate and <5ms p95 delta for canary.

sara (observability): also record a telemetry delta metric: compat.shim.injected.count and compat.client.warned.count. add a log line that surfaces tenant ID + injected header so support can contact customers. keep retention for 90 days.

max (ops): security review: ensure shim cannot be exploited to route requests to deprecated handlers or bypass auth. @camille can you add a short security checklist? I'll schedule the review once you file the RFC follow-up.

camille (arch): will do. i'll include config flags: edge.feature.inject_compat, runtime.accept_compat_header, telemetry keys, rollout plan, and rollback thresholds. i'll also add the exact response warning header: `X-RI-Compat-Warn: this endpoint will be removed in 180d; add X-RI-API-V to avoid compatibility injection`

lee (eng-infra): one more operational note: trace sampling for shim-injected requests should be higher (5%) so we can quickly triage regressions.

raj (runtime): agree. also add a health-check endpoint for the shim so we can tie its health to routing. don't put heavy logic in that health-check.

sara (observability): noted. @max i'll need a short runbook snippet for support: how to detect a tenant stuck on shim and how to reach out (email + support playbook).

max (ops): ok i'll draft the runbook after the RFC doc. i'll own the canary next week.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: edge-shim v0.3 -> eu-edge-1 (canary id 5973)

camille (arch): RFC follow-up created: https://redwood.internal/docs/arch/compat-edge-shim (contains telemetry keys, code snippets, timelines, canary plan). I'll also add the replay set link.

lee (eng-infra): thanks. sounds like consensus: deploy shim behind FF + telemetry + 180d deprecation. keep kill-switch.

raj (runtime): i'll add tests + harness PR today.

sara (observability): i'll wire metrics and the warning header.

max (ops): scheduling security review and the canary. ping me if anything changes. :thumbsup:
